parsed.explanation: The state/province adds meaningful visitor-facing protections: public-accommodations nondiscrimination is in force, and shield laws protect people travelling in for gender-affirming care. Its record does not establish how reliably service complaints are remedied, and these protections cannot override the national layer. National entry guidance permits refusal and demands for further evidence when an applicant’s sex or documents raise doubt; the consequences can include denial of entry, with lifetime ineligibility possible only under additional conditions. National restrictions on gender-congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities also remain an exposure, while the scale of their application to visitors here is unclear. National custody practices are a serious risk if detention occurs, not evidence of routine targeting of visitors. I therefore rate this above the national baseline, but below reduced risk. Uncertainty about facility scope is not itself evidence of safety.
